rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that believers will see their Lord, a report Biqāʿī uses to explain the verse’s language of vision.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( إنكم ترون ربكم ) فالاسم المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says the verse uses “Lord” for vision because the name Allah connotes the unseen and is associated here with loss rather than attainment.
rows.anchor: فالاسم المذكور لمعنى الرؤية إنما هو الرب لما في اسم الله تعالى من الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses taking as grasping an entire thing with force and violence.
rows.anchor: من الأخذ وهو تناول الشيء بجملته بنوع بطش وقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One unnamed reported view interprets the thunderbolt as a cry.
rows.anchor: أي لقولكم هذا لما فيه من الفظاعة وانتهاك الحرمة , { الصاعقة } قيل : هي صيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes it fire descending from heaven and burning them; Biqāʿī favors it because the verse says they were watching.
rows.anchor: قيل : نار نزلت من السماء فأحرقتهم , ويؤيده قوله { وأنتم تنظرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were killed for demanding vision in a manner resembling the calf worshippers, whom God had also killed.
rows.anchor: لأنكم كنتم في طلبكم رؤيته على ضرب من حال عبدة العجل , فأماتكم كما أماتهم بالقتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the thunderbolt killed them, God revived them by His greatness; this resurrection was an extraordinary return to earthly life.
rows.anchor: { ثم بعثناكم } أي بما لنا من العظمة بالإحياء

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines resurrection as arousing from hiddenness, strongest from graves and lesser from sleep.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : من البعث وهو الاستثارة من غيب وخفاء , أشده البعث من القبور , ودونه البعث من النوم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says “then” signals a long, extended interval; here it also alludes to Moses asking God to revive them lest their people be put to trial.
rows.anchor: قال : وتجاوز الخطاب ما كان من سبب بعثهم , وكذلك كل موضع يقع فيه ثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit phrase “after your death” confirms that they truly died, and their return did not end the obligations of earthly life, where deeds and remembrance purify the heart.
rows.anchor: { من بعد موتكم } أي هذا بتلك الصاعقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose is that their state become one in which gratitude for this immense favor may reasonably be hoped for; divine “perhaps” language should be understood similarly.
rows.anchor: { لعلكم تشكرون } أي لتصير حالكم حال من يصح ترجي شكره لهذه النعمة العظيمة

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī notes that replacing “perhaps you will give thanks” with “so that you give thanks” would remove the element of doubt.
rows.anchor: ولو قيل : لتشكروا , لم يكن هناك شك - قاله الرماني في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī reads “perhaps” as indicating that some of them would be grateful and others would not.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وفي لعل , إبهام معلومه فيهم بأن منهم من يشكر ومنهم من لا يشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Together with the earlier warning that no soul can avail another, this account warns Arabs who deny resurrection and directs them to ask the People of the Book about their ancestors’ revival and other resurrection stories.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية وما تقدمها من آية { واتقوا يوما لا تجزي نفس } تنبيه للعرب

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī treats this revival as proof of the promised universal resurrection: what happened to one person or a group can happen to all humankind.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وفيه أي هذا الخطاب آية على البعث الآخر الذي وعد به جنس بني آدم كلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of cloud shade naturally follows the thunderbolt, warning of its burning while recalling preservation from the sun’s heat and from hunger.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكرت الصاعقة الناشئة غالبا من الغمام كان أنسب الأشياء إيلاءها ذكر تظليل الغمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī presents passages from the second and third books of the Torah as testimony to Israel’s covenant and its commandments.
rows.anchor: ذكر ما يشهد لذلك من التوراة , قال في السفر الثاني منها لما ذكر أمر المناجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second book recalls God bringing Israel from Egyptian slavery and commands exclusive worship, rejection of idols and false oaths, honoring parents, and abstaining from murder, adultery, theft, false witness, and coveting; it also promises mercy to those who love and obey God.
rows.anchor: أنا الرب إلهك الذي أصعدتك من أرض مصر من العبودية والرق , لا تكون لك آلهة غيري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah passage says the people heard sounds and saw lights at the mountain revelation.
rows.anchor: وكان جميع الشعب يسمعون الأصوات ويرون المصابيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third-book passage forbids theft, treachery, false oaths, oppression, insulting the mute, and placing obstacles before the blind.
rows.anchor: لا تسرقوا , ولا تغدروا , ولا تحلفوا باسمي كذبا , ولا تنجسوا اسم الرب إلهكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It commands impartial justice for poor and great alike, honest rebuke instead of hatred, and love of one’s neighbor as oneself.
rows.anchor: لا تحابين المسكين ولا تحاب الكبير أيضا بل أقض بالبر والعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further commands reject divination and certain mourning and grooming customs, require honor for elders, kindness to resident outsiders, and honest weights and measures.
rows.anchor: لا تتبعوا العرافين والقافة ولا تنطلقوا إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The law says not to wrong a resident outsider but to treat them as one of the community, recalling Israel’s own time as outsiders in Egypt.
rows.anchor: وإذا سكن بينكم الذي يقبل إلي فلا تظلموه بل أنزلوه منزلة أحدكم وصيروه منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah requires fair courts, honest weights and measures, and preservation of God’s commands.
rows.anchor: لا تأثموا في القضاء ولا تأثموا في الأوزان والمكاييل بل اتخذوا ميزان الحق واتخذوا مكاييل الحق

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī derives dunya from lowliness: worldly life is lower in rank, immediate, and opposed to the higher, delayed afterlife.
rows.anchor: ففي الدنيا نزول قدر وتعجل وفي ا لأخرى علو قدر وتأخر , فتقابلتا على ما يفهم تقابلين من معنى كل واحدة منهما - قاله الحرالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired terms work by reciprocal ellipsis: mentioning worldly life implies the omitted “higher” life, while mentioning the afterlife implies the omitted “immediate” one.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتكاك , ذكر الدنيا أولا يدل على حذف العليا ثانيا , وذكر الآخرة ثانيا يدل على حذف العاجلة أولا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines alleviation as making something heavy and low become buoyant and elevated, like a stone rising into air.
rows.anchor: من التخفيف وهو مصير الثقيل والمستفل إلى حال الطافي المستعلي كحال ما بين الحجر والهواء - قاله الحرالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who trade the afterlife for worldly gain receive no reduction of punishment in either abode and no one can help them.
rows.anchor: { عنهم العذاب } في واحدة من الدارين { ولا هم ينصرون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their lack of help is a grave warning against campaigning for booty or committing embezzlement of spoils.
rows.anchor: وهو أيضا من أعظم الأدلة على خذلان من غزا لأجل المغنم أو غل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that when embezzlement of spoils appears among a people, God casts fear into their hearts; Biqāʿī transmits it from Ibn ʿAbbās through Mālik.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( ما ظهر الغلول في قوم إلا ألقى الله في قلوبهم الرعب )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī cites the story of Joshua: after Israel stole devoted spoils at Jericho, its troops were defeated at Ai; Achan was exposed by lot and stoned and burned with his household and property, after which Ai fell.
rows.anchor: فأصابت القرعة عاجار بن كرمى من سبط يهودا , فأحضره وبنيه وبناته ومواشيه وخيمته وكل من كان له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After showing Israel had broken its covenants and deserved lasting punishment, Biqāʿī frames the next verse as answering whether their failure came from ignorance or defiance.
rows.anchor: توقع السائل الإخبار عن سبب وقوعهم في ذلك هل هو جهل أو عناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Moses the Torah, which Israel still possessed and studied, so they had not been left without guidance after him.
rows.anchor: مع أن عندكم فيها كتاب الله التوراة تدرسونه كل حين , فلم ندعكم هملا بعد موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī explains qaffaynā as making one thing follow another, like successive tracks or the back of an image.
rows.anchor: من التقفية وهي متابعة شيء شيئا كأنه يتلو فقاه , وفقاء الصورة منها خلفها المقابل الموجه - قاله الحرالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent prophets successively after Moses to renew religious teaching and reinforce Israel’s covenant, beyond the guidance already preserved in the Torah.
rows.anchor: بل واترنا من بعده إرسال الرسل مواترة , وجعلنا بعضهم في قفاء بعض ليجددوا لكم أمر الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī notes that ʿĪsā is an Arabized name whose original form is Yashūʿ.
rows.anchor: { عيسى } اسم معرب . أصله يسوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus was sent to abrogate some of the Torah and renew what had been effaced from the rest.
rows.anchor: الذي أرسلناه لنسخ بعض التوراة تجديد ما درس من بقيتها

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī glosses the clear signs as extraordinary proofs so evident that a rational person cannot dispute them.
rows.anchor: والبينة من القول والكون ما لا ينازعه منازع لوضوحه - قاله الحرالي

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī derives divine strengthening from strength, likening it to a helping hand or support from the back, the seat of a thing’s inherent power.
rows.anchor: كأخذ قوة المظاهرة من الظهر , لأن الظهر موضع قوة الشيء في ذاته , واليد موضع قوة تناوله لغيره - قاله الحرالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Holy Spirit is the pure spirit Gabriel, with whom God also strengthened other resolute prophets.
rows.anchor: أي الروح الطاهر وهو جبريل عليه السلام كما أيدنا به غيره من أولي العزم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the spirit is a glimpse of God’s command, which sustains creation; the spirit of an individual is a glimpse of that command.
rows.anchor: وما هو قوام صورة من جملة الخلق هو الروح الذي هو لمحة من ذلك الأمر

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says spirits sustain the created realm through the unseen and the enduring religious order; Gabriel’s spirit serves religious command, while Israfil’s serves the bodily blast.
rows.anchor: ومن أخص الروح به جبريل عليه السلام بما له من روح الأمر الديني , وإسرافيل عليه السلام بما له من روح النفخ الصوري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus had a special association with the Spirit because he raised many dead people to life.
rows.anchor: وقد كان لعيسى عليه السلام بالروح مزيد اختصاص لكثرة ما أحيى من الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite the successive prophets and signs, Israel continued breaking its covenants and then failed to affirm Muhammad.
rows.anchor: والمعنى فعلنا بكم يا بني إسرائيل ذلك ولم تزالوا في عهد جميع من ذكر ناقضين للعهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī introduces a composite citation from the four Gospels, combining their wording and drawing mostly on Matthew, as evidence of Jesus’s signs and support by the Holy Spirit.
rows.anchor: ذكر شيء من الإنجيل يدل على أنه عليه السلام أتى بالبينات مع تأييده بروح القدس مستخلصا من الأناجيل الأربعة وقد جمعت بين ألفاظها

rows.speaker: متى
rows.claim: Matthew says Jesus moved to Galilee and settled in Capernaum after John was handed over, fulfilling Isaiah’s prophecy about Zebulun, Naphtali, and a great light dawning on people in darkness.
rows.anchor: قال متى - ومعظم السياق له : فلما سمع يسوع أن يوحنا

rows.speaker: متى
rows.claim: Matthew’s account has Jesus announce that the time is fulfilled and God’s kingdom is near, calling people to repent and believe the Gospel.
rows.anchor: جليل يكرز بإنجيل ملكوت الله قائلا : قد كمل الزمان وقربت ملكوت الله ! فتوبوا وآمنوا بالإنجيل

rows.speaker: متى
rows.claim: Matthew says Jesus called the fishermen Simon Peter and Andrew, then James and John, to follow him and become fishers of people; they immediately left their nets, boat, and father.
rows.anchor: قال متى : وكان يمشي على بحر الجليل فأبصر أخوين سمعان الذي يدعى بطرس واندراوس أخاه يلقيان شباكهما في البحر

rows.speaker: إنجيل يوحنا
rows.claim: The John Gospel passage calls Jesus the Lamb of God who removes the world’s sin, says he existed before John, and says John baptized with water to reveal him to Israel.
rows.anchor: وفي إنجيل يوحنا بعد قصة يحيى بن زكريا الآتية في آل عمران : هذا كان في بيت عينا في عبر الأردن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Continuing the John Gospel account, John testifies that the Spirit descended from heaven like a dove and remained on Jesus; the one who sent John to baptize with water identified Jesus as the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.
rows.anchor: وقال : إني رأيت الروح نزل من السماء مثل حمامة وحل عليه ولم أعرفه , لكن من أرسلني لأعمد بالماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the continuing John Gospel account, two of John’s disciples follow Jesus; Andrew finds his brother Simon and identifies Jesus as the Messiah, and Jesus names Simon Cephas, meaning Peter.
rows.anchor: فسمع تلميذاه كلامه فتبعا يسوع , فالتفت يسوع فرآهما يتبعانه فقال لهما : ماذا تريدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus tells Philip that Moses and the prophets wrote of him; Nathanael doubts that anything good could come from Nazareth, but Jesus recognizes him under a fig tree and Nathanael calls him Israel’s king.
rows.anchor: الذي كتب موسى من أجله في الناموس والأنبياء وجدناه وهو يسوع الذي من الناصرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus tells Nathanael that he will witness greater things, including heaven opened and God’s angels ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.
rows.anchor: الحق الحق أقول لكم , إنكم من الآن ترون السماء مفتحة وملائكة الله ينزلون ويصعدون على ابن البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Cana, Jesus turns water in six stone jars used for Jewish purification into wine, his first sign, displaying his glory and leading his disciples to believe in him.
rows.anchor: وكان هناك ستة أجاجين من حجارة موضوعة لتطهير اليهود تسع كل واحدة مطرين أو ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The John Gospel account says the steward praises the bridegroom for saving the better wine until now; this was Jesus’s first sign at Cana, and his disciples believed.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية الأولى التي فعلها يسوع في قانا الجليل وأظهر مجده وآمن به تلاميذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus leaves Judea for Galilee after hearing that the Pharisees know he has more disciples than John, passing through Samaria.
rows.anchor: وعلم السيد يسوع أن الفريسيين سمعوا أنه قد اتخذ تلاميذ كثيرة وأنه يعمد أكثر من يوحنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Jacob’s well, Jesus asks a Samaritan woman for water; she questions the request because Jews do not associate with Samaritans, and he offers her living water.
rows.anchor: فقالت له تلك المرأة : كيف وأنت يهودي تستقي الماء وأنا امرأة سامرية واليهود لا يختلطون بالسامرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus says those who drink his water will never thirst; he reveals that the woman had five husbands and her current partner is not her husband, leading her to recognize him as a prophet.
rows.anchor: لأنه قد كان لك خمسة بعولة والذي هو لك الآن ليس هو زوجك , أما هذا فحقا قلت , قالت : يا سيد ! إني أرى أنك نبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asked whether worship belongs on the Samaritan mountain or in Jerusalem, Jesus says the coming hour will be neither place and that true worshippers worship the Father in spirit and truth.
rows.anchor: ستأتي ساعة لا في هذا الجبل ولا في يروشليم يسجدون للأب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Samaritan woman says the Messiah will come and teach everything; Jesus identifies himself to her, and she leaves her jar to tell the town, prompting people to come see him.
rows.anchor: قالت المرأة : قد علمت أن مسيا الذي هو المسيح يأتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus says his food is to do the will of the one who sent him and complete that work.
rows.anchor: فقال : طعامي أنا أن أعمل مسرة من أرسلني وأتم عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus uses a ripe-field harvest image: reapers earn their wage and gather fruit for eternal life; sower and reaper rejoice together, and his disciples reap work done by others.
rows.anchor: ارفعوا أعينكم وانظروا إلى الكور قد ابيضت وبلغت الحصاد , والذي يحصد يأخذ الأجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many Samaritans first believe because of the woman and then because they hear Jesus themselves; after he stays two days, they confess him as the world’s Savior.
rows.anchor: فآمن به كثير , وكانوا يقولون للمرأة : لسنا من أجل قولك نؤمن به لكنا قد سمعنا وعلمنا أن هذا هو المسيح بالحقيقة مخلص العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus leaves for Galilee, saying a prophet is not honored in his own town; Galileans nonetheless welcome him because they saw his works in Jerusalem during the festival.
rows.anchor: لأنه شهد أن النبي لا يكرم في مدينته , ولما صار إلى الجليل قبله الجليليون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus heals a royal official’s son near death from a distance, at the seventh hour; the official believes his word before seeing the result, and the Gospel calls it his second sign in Galilee.
rows.anchor: فعلم أبوه أنه في تلك الساعة التي قال له يسوع فيها : إن ابنك قد حيي , فآمن هو وبيته بأسره

rows.speaker: مرقس
rows.claim: Mark says Jesus taught in Capernaum’s synagogue on the Sabbath, and the people were amazed because he taught with authority.
rows.anchor: قال مرقس : فأقبل غلى كفرناحوم وبقي يعلم في مجامعهم يوم السبت , فتعجبوا من تعليمه لأنه كان كالمسلط

words: مَا نَنسَخْ مِنْ ءَايَةٍ أَوْ نُنسِهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī treats God’s prohibition of “raʿinā” after previously allowing it as an instance of abrogation.
rows.anchor: ولما حرم سبحانه قوله { راعنا } بعد حله وكان ذلك من باب النسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrogation transfers a benefit, such as property, religion, power, or knowledge, from one people to another after God’s favor selects them.
rows.anchor: بعد التخصيص الذي من مقتضاه نقل ما يكون من المنافع من ملك أو دين أو قوة أو علم من ناس إلى ناس

rows.speaker: اليهود
rows.claim: The Jews claim their religion cannot be abrogated, arguing that abrogation would imply badāʾ, or God’s learning something only after it appears.
rows.anchor: وكان اليهود يرون أن دينهم لا ينسخ , فكان النسخ لذلك من مطاعنهم في هذا الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī answers that the Torah itself contains abrogation: after Israel refused to fight the giants and enter Jerusalem, God forbade their entry and fighting.
rows.anchor: فإن فيه أنه تعالى أمرهم بالدخول إلى بيت المقدس بعد مقاتلة الجبارين , فلما أبوا حرم عليهم دخولها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says the Jews were commanded to observe Friday but disputed about it and chose Saturday, after which the Sabbath was imposed strictly; the Qur’an also states this.
rows.anchor: وأمرهم بالجمعة فاختلفوا فيه , كما قاله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another Torah example is that all meats and fats were initially permitted, then fats were forbidden to Israel after they worshipped the calf.
rows.anchor: واختاروا السبت , ففرض عليهم وشدد عليهم فيه وأحل لهم جميع اللحوم والشحوم , لما اتخذوا العجل حرم عليهم الشحوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī calls the greater unauthorized alteration a false form of abrogation: religious scholars distort scripture and forbid or permit whatever rulings they wish.
rows.anchor: وأعظم من ذلك تعاطيهم من النسخ ما لم يأذن به الله في تحريفهم الكلم عن مواضعه
